messages:
incident-bot: [P1] High 5xx & latency spike detected for inference-prod-usw2a. Alert window: 00:04. Error rate up ~22% vs baseline. Auto-runbook attached: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-egress-degrad
aws-alert-bot: VPC flow samples show a sharp increase in retransmits and RSTs from proxy fleet in us-west-2a -> natgw-0a0b0c. Route table rtb-0deadbeef shows a 'blackhole' for main-egress route (local to usw2a).
jordan: I'm paged. joining. What's the scope? any customer-facing reports yet?
maria: I see elevated 502 and TLS handshake timeouts on host-proxy-g5-* in us-west-2a. Model loads are stuck during TLS due to handshake timeouts to model-storage (S3) and auth to KMS occasionally failing. Could be egress/NAT path causing packet loss.
jordan: running quick curl test against /v1/generate endpoint from a scratch instance in same subnet:
```
$ time curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://inference.prod.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
...
real    2m10.234s
```
lee: I can repro from a different AZ (us-west-2b) and it's fine. So likely single-AZ egress problem.
maria: VPC Flow Log peek (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T16:12:01Z eni-0f1a2b3c 10.10.10.5 52.95.12.34 443 56784 REJECT
2026-03-15T16:12:01Z eni-0f1a2b3c 10.10.10.5 52.95.12.34 443 56784 ACCEPT
... (retransmit spikes)
```
jordan: ok immediate mitigation plan options: 1) enable cross-zone routing at ALB and shift traffic away from nodes in us-west-2a; 2) programmatic failover: mark target-group unhealthy for us-west-2a nodes; 3) scale up us-west-2b/c and shift routing via router rules. Also product mitigation: switch heavy customer tenants to quantized small-model fallback to reduce backend TLS load.
tara (cust-success): we have an enterprise customer (acme) reporting elevated errors for inference calls. They asked for ETA. we should send interim customer note after initial mitigation.
lee: I'll start shifting 30% traffic with weighted routing to us-west-2b. Starting small canary first.
maria: I'm going to drain model loads on g5 instances in usw2a and force model cache drop to reduce stuck loads. command: ``kubectl -n inference cordon node g5-node-123 && kubectl -n inference drain g5-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``
support-bot: Noted. Posting customer notification draft channel #support-digest in 5.
jordan: monitor: creating a canary curl test to a /healthz and sending p95/p99 logs to #incidents. Running canary now.
lee: canary (10 requests) -> 10/10 OK via us-west-2b. switching 10% traffic now. Will watch error-rate.
jordan: I see error-rate drop from 22% -> 12% after initial 10% shift. Good signal.
maria: NAT gateway metrics: nat-0a0b0c CPU low but active connections high and connection tracking entries spiked. AWS console shows state 'impaired' for the natgw in subnet-a.
aws-alert-bot: AWS reports degraded route propagation in rtb-0deadbeef; possible transient route table health issue in AZ us-west-2a. AWS support case opened: case 1234567890.
jordan: escalation: spin up replacement nat in us-west-2a (nat-0repl) and update route table to point 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0repl. maria, can you handle env IAM pieces for creating replacement NAT? lee, hold on traffic shift to 40% only after we verify new nat.
maria: creating replacement NAT now. Steps:
- allocate new EIP
- create NAT gateway in subnet-a
- wait for available state
- modify route table
I expect 8-12 mins.
lee: copying. holding further shifts to 40% until new NAT in place.
support-bot: Customer note v1 drafted: "We're investigating a single-AZ egress issue in us-west-2 causing intermittent 502s for inference. We're actively failing over traffic and will provide updates in 15 minutes." Ready for review.
tara (cust-success): send to Acme and cc their TAM. Mark as interim.
jordan: new NAT is provisioned (nat-0repl). Modifying route table now.
maria: route table updated. small window of reflow observed.
aws-alert-bot: Connectivity checks show reduced RSTs from proxy fleet. TCP handshake times decreased.
lee: increasing traffic weight to 60% now. monitoring.
jordan: p95 token latency back down to baseline, error-rate <1.5% now. Good.
support-bot: Sent customer interim update to Acme. They asked to be informed when fully resolved.
maria: leaving nagios checks for NAT health and conntrack below threshold. added autoscale rule to spawn helper proxy pods if conntrack>80%.
jordan: thanks team. I'll keep incident declared until 2h post-stable.
incident-bot: Incident declared: P1 -> partial mitigation achieved. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-egress-degrad. Incident lead: jordan. Severity start 4087654321.
lee: handing to maria for ongoing cleanup and postmortem prep. I'm heading offline for next rotation. :wave:
maria: taking over oncall. will collect logs, save tcpdump samples, and open postmortem draft. Action items: 1) postmortem, 2) confirm automatic replacement NAT behavior, 3) review model-loading retry/backoff to avoid stuck TLS connections.
jordan: thanks. final check: confirm all enterprise tenants back to normal. tara, please send a confirm note once Acme confirms.
tara (cust-success): Acme acked receipt of interim and says errors reduced. will confirm when fully validated.
maria: creating postmortem stub and will tag owners. timeline and RCA to follow.
support-bot: Closing customer interim loop. Will update channel when final note sent.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE] Service returned to normal and error-rate stable for 30m. Declaring operationally resolved. Resolution notes: route table route to impaired NAT replaced, traffic shifted, model-fallback available if needed. Incident closed 4087669800."
